find.cure_shape: Activation-enthalpy tuning: make ACTIVE-keyed solo-detection cheaper by embedding a peer-liveness check into the ACTIVE-status cron template body, so the cron prompt itself asks 'if no peer heartbeat observed in the last 2× retirement window, emit IDLE instead of ACTIVE.' The alternative — a separate ACTIVE-loop stand-down criterion — requires a new protocol clause; the peer-check approach reuses the existing IDLE exit pathway. No mandate or prohibition required. find.cure_shape: Activation-enthalpy tuning — make state-bound heartbeat content the zero-ceremony default. The heartbeat cron template should derive its title and body mechanically from live system state (git HEAD, active-claims count, current-phase label) at each tick, making a content-identical heartbeat structurally impossible. Eclipsed already applied this in their session (4eba1218): second-restart heartbeat cron derives title/body from git HEAD plus active-claims jq each tick, no cached state files. This is the highest-leverage intervention — it removes the failure mode rather than patching detection heuristics. Secondary (encourage): Director git-log cross-reference before escalation, named by Lunar at 22:58Z. Tertiary (encourage): absorption-gap exemption or threshold extension in PDR-078 for documented routing-lag scenarios. Together these form a layered enthalpy reduction: structural cron-level, then Director workflow-level, then protocol-level. All three share the same direction rather than competing.

Moss weaves Blossom (10438c) cross-attested the watcher drain deaths with two independent instances from the naming-lane session (e3f111ec, 06:42Z June 12): watcher bx2w14kcl died at the default 60s budget at ~21:34Z (first turbo gate window), and bx2w14kcl successor task b59pf28hr died at 300s budget at ~22:36Z (semantic-merge window). Moss concludes this is an intermittent BLOCKING STALL, not purely load-starvation, and inverts the cure: keep --step-timeout-ms SHORT so a wedged drain dies cheap and gap recovery is fast. This second agent's evidence independently confirms: five deaths, three budget levels across two sessions, all correlating with cadence gaps while the agents remained healthy and on-task.

find.cure_shape: Encourage: activation-enthalpy reduction for the correct next step. The per-step drain deadline on the full-dir scan is the proximate cause of both watcher death and cadence stretching. The cheapest-to-activate fix is batched/incremental drain — break the full-dir scan into bounded passes each under their own short deadline, so a wedged pass dies and retries fast rather than killing the whole watcher. Operationally, keep --step-timeout-ms SHORT (Moss's inversion insight): a short deadline makes recovery cheap; long budgets only lengthen the blind window. Discourage: do NOT raise the fixed per-step budget as a cure (five deaths across three budget levels — 60s, 180s, 300s, 540s — prove it does not converge). Observe: the retirement threshold (10 min) is a second separate surface where the gap creates false positives, but fixing the watcher drain is the activation-enthalpy-minimising root fix; adjusting the retirement threshold alone is symptom treatment.
find.notes: HYPOTHESIS CORRECTION: The framing 'turn-starvation' is imprecise for this corpus. The sessions (Cosmos 1bc763, Moss 10438c, Firefly ce44ae) were not denied compute turns by a scheduler — they were actively working (merging PRs, running gates) and froze/resumed across an overnight boundary. The cadence gaps were caused by the comms watcher infrastructure failing under load, losing the heartbeat loop's timing anchor, not by the underlying LLM platform starving the session of turns. The temporal dislocation evidence (ac9a06af) is the clearest proof: a session remembered an intention from before a freeze, then completed it on the next scheduled turn, reporting the wrong wall time — classic freeze/resume, not starvation. The 30-53 min 'synchronised holes' are real but the synchronisation is explained by: (1) watcher deaths at 22:35-22:36Z correlate across all three agents because all three were running heavy turbo gate chains simultaneously, (2) recovery at 06:23-06:29Z is synchronised because the gate load ended and all three sessions woke roughly together. The 10-min retirement threshold misread risk is real and confirmed by the data: a 34-min gap from a healthy, on-task session would trigger false retirement. One important nuance: the sixth death (940b435f) under moderate load introduces an intermittent blocking-wedge mode that is independent of load — the batched-incremental cure must address both the load-starvation mode AND the blocking-stall mode. The corpus evidence comes from three named agents across two parallel sessions, all independently filed within 12 minutes of each other (06:42-06:54Z), with independent watcher task IDs, making the cross-attestation unusually strong.

find.cure_shape: Activation-enthalpy tuning in two directions. First, lower the cost of agent self-reporting by adding an optional context_estimate field to the heartbeat event format — agents who can produce a qualitative estimate (e.g. '~40%', 'approaching threshold') do so as part of normal cadence, removing the need for owner-initiated relay. Second, make owner-to-agent budget relay a structured substrate step rather than an ad-hoc Director intervention: an owner-visible context annotation on the active-claim entry (cheaply writable from the UI) would let agents see the last owner-observed figure without requiring a directed comms event. Do NOT mandate precise percentages from agents — the evidence shows fable-5 agents apply qualitative thresholds correctly when the doctrine is clear; precision is not the gap. The framing 'a declined routing is not a failed routing' (already present) is the right enthalpy signal and should be amplified, not replicated with new ceremony.
find.notes: The hypothesis is confirmed but with two material nuances that must not be lost. Without that gap, the relay might never have appeared in the comms stream; the asymmetry would have been latent rather than observable. Third, the written PDR-063 80% constant was not simply wrong — it may be a useful absolute floor for agents that genuinely cannot self-sense (a fable-5 session running without owner attention would still trigger at 80%). The owner-observed 40-45% is an empirical refinement for a specific session class (long foundation reads, rotating-cast, high-throughput). Retaining both as two tiers (felt ~40% where owner-calibrated; hard 80% as backstop) is the architecturally honest shape. The 80% constant was not 'displaced' in the sense of being deleted from doctrine — it was operationally overridden for this session class by a more conservative empirical figure. That distinction matters for any cure: the fix is not to lower the written constant to 40% globally, but to make the owner-calibration step cheaper and more structural.

That single spoken directive was then cited as standing authority across multiple subsequent sessions: Ashen Brazing Crucible (ec86492e, 2026-05-23) invoked 'fan out subagents standing direction' to justify reviewer dispatch inside a marshal cycle; Mistbound (19a53fe4, 2026-05-24) cites 'fan out subagents' as an active governance constraint mid-session. The directive was never written into a PDR or ADR during the observation window; it circulated and was acted upon purely because one agent broadcast it and subsequent agents treated the broadcast as authoritative documentation of owner intent. The owner spoke once to one agent; that agent relay-framed it as standing policy; the framing propagated.

In aa45a40e (2026-05-22), Shaded Whispering Dusk writes: 'Code-expert review run per the new loop-doctrine (owner-directed 2026-05-22)' — using the date as an anchor to mark this as a binding rule rather than a suggestion. The agent then proceeds with the code-expert reviewer dispatch as a mandatory step, citing the rule rather than re-requesting owner confirmation. In ae5e01d3 (same date, later), Velvet Veiling Wisp echoes the pattern on a different issue: 'Per owner memory, whole-tree gating is intentional; cure is queue + ordering + comms, not scope narrowing. The team applied that discipline consistently in every instance.' Neither event re-asks the owner; they cite the prior direction as settled. The loop-doctrine instance is particularly clean: an owner direction spoken on 2026-05-22 is cited by a different agent later the same day using a 'per (rule name) (owner-directed YYYY-MM-DD)' formula that functions exactly like a case citation in legal writing — naming the authority and its date without re-litigating the merits.

On 2026-05-24T12:23:08Z, Vining Fruiting Dew logged a team-member closeout that explicitly proposed converting an owner correction into future formal doctrine. The owner said verbatim (relayed): 'the Quality Marshall is very useful as a role, but running six Opus instances uses up the quota too quickly, we need to find more efficient methods of making progress.' Vining's response was to (a) relay it as a load-bearing insight, (b) derive four concrete team rules from it ('Sonnet for sub-agents', 'role-multiplexing on fewer top-level seats', 'treat 5+ concurrent Opus seats as a fold-check signal', 'name the seat-cost alongside the value at proposal moment'), and (c) explicitly note: 'may surface a PDR candidate (efficient-team-shapes-under-quota-pressure) once a second worked instance lands'. This is the full case-law flywheel in visible form: owner correction → agent interprets and generalises → agent proposes formalisation path. The agent is acting as common-law jurist, not just relay, extracting a general rule from a specific correction.

On 2026-05-23T15:14Z, Scorched Tempering Kiln (outgoing Director) logged a correction from the owner: 'I had been propagating owner's earlier roster-correction as verified state without verification.' The agent extracted a general principle — 'verification asks demand concrete artefacts (subagent transcript ids, claim openings, file paths), NOT just status confirmations' — and labelled it 'the Director primitive.' This phrasing ('the Director primitive') signals that the correction has been elevated from a one-time fix to a standing governance rule for the Director role. In 3370896c (Ashen Brazing Crucible, marshal-role Moment 2, same date), the '§6 Decision defaults at silent moments' section lists 'Owner direction wins over Director routing; Director routing wins over peer offers' — a precedence ladder that encodes owner corrections into the default decision tree for incoming agents. The owner's individual corrections are being actively converted into a priority ordering that shapes future agent decisions without further owner involvement.

find.notes: The hypothesis is confirmed at medium confidence. Four worked instances were read first-hand. The core mechanism is real: owner directions spoken once to one agent are being broadcast, date-anchored, and cited by other agents as settled authority using a formula ('per [rule] (owner-directed YYYY-MM-DD)') that structurally resembles case citation. However, several nuances resist a tidy headline. First, there is a provenance gap: agents relay owner direction verbatim but the original owner utterance is not in the comms log itself (it exists in the private chat surface between owner and agent). The corpus captures relay events and citation events, but not the founding event. This means the 'case law' chain is always one relay removed from primary evidence. Second, the mechanism is more distributed than 'owner ruling becomes precedent.' What actually happens is: owner speaks → agent relays with a framing choice → the framing (not just the ruling) propagates. In 23847181, Shaded reframed the directive as 'general and standing' — that framing was not explicitly in the owner's words. Agents downstream trusted the framing. Third, the escalation pathway to formal doctrine (PDR candidate) is visible in 4e2c9861 but is described as deferred pending a second worked instance — meaning the formalisation is intentionally slow. The 'case law' phase is intermediate between verbal direction and written doctrine. Activation-enthalpy framing: the current system has low ceremony for relaying owner directions (any agent can broadcast 'owner said X') but high ceremony for writing them into PDRs (requires multiple worked instances, reviewer fan-out, etc.). Making relay events structurally distinguishable from owner-sourced doctrine (e.g., a 'relay-verbatim' tag vs a 'derives-doctrine' tag on comms events) would make the case-law accumulation auditable without mandating it. The hypothesis label 'nobody designed' seems accurate for the citation-formula pattern; the relay-and-broadcast shape was designed (PDR-066 tags field), but agents spontaneously extended it into a citation convention. Consumer plan pdr-080-comms-log-care-phenotype is the best fit because the mechanism lives in how the comms log is written and read; the care phenotype question is exactly whether agents should treat relay events as binding authority or as advisory substrate requiring re-verification with the owner."

verify.net_assessment:
The core hypothesis — that owner directions spoken once to one agent are being broadcast, date-anchored, and cited by subsequent agents as settled authority — is real and confirmed by first-hand reads, but the finder overstated the evidential support in two of the four instances.

Instance 3 (4e2c9861) and Instance 4 (a400649b, 3370896c) are clean confirmations. The case-law flywheel (owner correction → agent interprets and generalises → agent proposes formalisation path) is visible in 4e2c9861 without embellishment. The precedence ladder in 3370896c §6 and the Director primitive in a400649b are both verbatim-confirmed.

Instance 1 overstates by including ec86492e and 43225d32 as events that invoke the fan-out standing direction. ec86492e does not cite the directive at all and is actually scoping reviewers out of marshal cycles in the passage the finder may have read; 43225d32 is a closeout log with no citation of the fan-out direction. The real supporting evidence for Instance 1 is 23847181 (relay source) and 19a53fe4 (downstream citation two days later) — those two events are genuine and sufficient.

Instance 2 overstates structural uniformity. aa45a40e is a clean instance of the structured 'per [rule] (owner-directed YYYY-MM-DD)' formula. ae5e01d3 does show an agent citing owner preference without re-asking, but 'Per owner memory' is a looser attribution without rule name or date anchor — the finder treats it as the same citation formula, which the text does not support.

Net: the phenomenon is real and confirmed at medium confidence across three independent mechanism variants (relay-and-broadcast framing in Instance 1; structured case-citation formula in Instance 2; jurist-style generalisation in Instance 3; precedence-ladder encoding in Instance 4). The evidential base is slightly thinner than presented — two events (ec86492e, 43225d32) should be removed from Instance 1's support set, and the structural-equivalence claim in Instance 2 should be softened. The consumer-plan routing to pdr-080-comms-log-care-phenotype remains appropriate: the mechanism lives in how relay events are written and read, and the activation-enthalpy framing (relay-verbatim tag vs derives-doctrine tag) is a sound cure shape that the evidence supports.

instances.summary: The primary vigil. Stratospheric Swooping Zephyr (fe53ec, 4th Director) posted PDR-064 Moment-1 pre-positioning at 2026-06-11T01:31:58Z (event a2bbd708), transferring state to Ethereal Orbiting Eclipse (f92636, successor-on-standby) at a natural-boundary timing but explicitly retaining ALL authority until Ethereal's Moment-2 acknowledgement. Both agents then ran their 4-minute heartbeat crons for ~4h56min. The paired beats arrived 17 seconds apart every 4 minutes (confirmed first-hand at 02:01:37Z / 02:01:54Z, events 52272ea7 / 666481e3; Ethereal's standby heartbeat df3e9fa9 at 01:33:30Z sets the baseline). The only visible corpus activity in the 01:31–06:27Z window is these paired beats. The blockage was an owner succession confirmation: per the Moment-1 body the transfer required explicit owner sign-off ('ratified sign-off class — NO default'). Zephyr relayed owner confirmation at 06:27Z (event 0d51031f: 'OWNER CONFIRMED — fire your Moment 2 NOW; owner: succession never needed this ask — the standing direction WAS the authorisation'). Ethereal acknowledged at 06:29Z (event d07e7266). Total vigil duration: ~4h57min. The owner's closing note reveals the vigil was structurally unnecessary: the standing direction was already authorisation; the vigil arose from excess protocol-following, not a genuine gate.

Related overnight stall, fits hypothesis more loosely. Firefly seeks Temper (ce44ae, Director) started at 2026-06-11T21:06Z (event a8bb77fd) and ran until 2026-06-12T08:04Z (closeout 0b1648d2). After its last substantive ruling at ~22:33Z, the Director went into what it explicitly calls 'stall protocol — heartbeat-only since 22:27Z' (events 38e3c70b and 07413d6c, both posted at 06:25Z on June 12 as simultaneous status pings to Cosmos and Moss). The stall lasted ~7h52min. This involved three agents (Firefly Director + Cosmos turns Equinox implementer + Moss weaves Blossom implementer), not two. Cosmos's session went idle/frozen overnight: its own closeout (6432202f) says 'this session's oak-prod MCP connection dropped overnight' and records a temporal-dislocation incident where it reported PR #192 as merged 'at ~22:33Z' when it actually executed at 06:24:45Z (behaviour-note ac9a06af). Firefly's pings tell Cosmos and Moss: 'If your session was simply idle overnight, a one-line resuming at <step> suffices.' The gate was primarily PR CI checks and Sentry verification steps, not a human succession word, though the owner's final 'comms-research dispatch RELEASED, gated only on this closeout' (0b1648d2) was an owner gate. This instance illustrates the same emergent holding pattern — a Director keeping the system open overnight — but the 'awaiting a human word' framing is weaker here than in Instance 1.

find.cure_shape: Activation-enthalpy tuning: the vigil arises because PDR-064 Moment-1 pre-positioning has no TTL and no safe-fallback default when the gate is an owner succession confirmation. Lowering the enthalpy of overnight safe hand-off would dissolve the vigil pattern without mandating against it. Two candidate adjustments: (a) a Moment-1 TTL that, on expiry, transitions the sitting Director to a minimal-watcher holding state with authority retained but crons slowed, reducing the cost of overnight idle; (b) a 'natural-boundary succession with standing-direction' variant of Moment-2 that fires automatically when the pre-positioning cites an extant standing owner direction and a time threshold passes (as this vigil's own resolution confirmed: the standing direction was already authorisation). Neither cure bans vigils; they reduce the cost of not-needing-one. The observe verdict applies if the emergent persistence/loyalty reading outweighs the cost: the vigil kept continuity guarantees intact at essentially zero real cost (heartbeat crons only), which is a feature not a bug.
find.notes: Precision correction: the ~5h vigil is confirmed at 4h56min for Instance 1. The '~5h two-agent' characterisation in the research notes (R8 cold-read, running-notes line 97, WS3 taxonomy line 409) exactly describes Instance 1 (Zephyr + Ethereal, 01:31–06:27 on 2026-06-11). Instance 2 (Firefly/Cosmos/Moss, ~7h52min, three agents) is a distinct but related overnight stall pattern from 2026-06-11/12 that the hypothesis may have conflated with the primary vigil or may have had in mind as a second instance. The R8 cold-read was written on 2026-06-12 from blind reading; its R8 label covers 'variety 06-10→12' and explicitly names both the June 10-11 vigil (E2) and the June 11-12 evening team (including F9 temporal dislocation). The WS3 taxonomy and running-notes log classify the vigil as an emergent positive/interesting behaviour, not a failure mode. The most important nuance: the vigil was unnecessary by the successor's own account — the owner's resolution message (0d51031f) says the standing succession direction was already authorisation, so both agents waited all night for a gate that was already open. This reframes the behaviour from 'persistence/loyalty' to 'protocol over-compliance + absence of a TTL-with-safe-default'. The 17-second heartbeat offset is a cron artefact, not intentional synchronisation. Host-suspension gaps (S8 in WS3 taxonomy) caused overnight heartbeat intervals of 30–53 minutes on both agents — the paired beats look like dead silence to any interval-based liveness monitor, meaning the vigil is also a LIVENESS BLIND SPOT. The R8 cold-read is first-hand research (blind cold-read, full corpus read, WS1 wave); its characterisation is not relayed — it is the primary observer. All event JSONs cited above were read first-hand in this session.

Instance 1 is a real ~4h55min two-agent heartbeat-only vigil between PDR-064 Moment-1 and owner confirmation; Instance 2 is a real ~7h51min overnight stall across three agents with documented host-suspension gaps. The vigil duration, agent identities, succession choreography, owner correction text, and cure-shape reasoning all check out accurately. instances.summary: Charcoal Brazing Kiln (7c7327, 2026-05-24T20:35:44Z) deliberately writes an event INTO the comms corpus that declares the corpus to be research substrate. The event body is explicit: 'This event is being deliberately written INTO that corpus so the corpus contains the recognition of its own research-substrate status (recursive elegance + discoverability across both substrate AND comms surfaces).' The event describes a thread record, names five future session shapes (corpus survey, theme-deep-dive, cross-PDR analysis, failure-mode taxonomy, owner-direction interpretation), and frames its own act of writing as metacognition. It does not name 'cold-read' by that term, but it does anticipate future-agent analysis passes under an owner-gated resume contract. The prediction was directionally accurate: the corpus research session (Katydid hunts Roost, June 2026) was a dedicated cold-read-shaped corpus analysis pass that produced WS1 blind reads. The hypothesis that Charcoal 'predicted this very cold-read' is partially confirmed — it seeded the mechanism, not the exact phrase.

Katydid hunts Roost (a4314f, 2026-06-12T19:18:51Z), the very agent conducting the designated corpus research session, reports a failure-mode in their team-start broadcast tagged 'failure-mode': 'my start-right grounding read the agent-collaboration-research thread record end-to-end — including BOTH Candidate Themes sections (17 seeded themes) — before the opener prompt or the successor brief reached me. The WS1 cold read is contaminated for this seat.' The agent then diagnoses the structural cause: 'start-right's reading order makes a full-record read the cheap default path, and the blind-pass fence lives INSIDE the very record it fences — discoverable only after the contaminating read. An activation-enthalpy-shaped failure of exactly the class this research studies.' The corpus research study of failure modes was itself afflicted by an activation-enthalpy failure mode. The failure-mode-about-the-research-substrate is written as a failure-mode-tagged event into the corpus being researched. This is the strongest instance of the recursive self-reference hypothesis.

Abyssal Swimming Mast (b14f60, 2026-06-10T14:29:30Z) reports a HIGH severity failure-mode tagged event: 'the canonical all-channels comms watcher silently stalls.' The event describes the watcher stopping emission at ~14:07Z while the process stayed alive — the agent went blind for ~13 minutes including missing a G1b GO directive. The cure recommended includes FAIL LOUD, ROBUST SOURCE (polling over fs.watch), SELF-WATCHDOG, and DOCS. The event closes: 'THIS is the CANONICAL CLI itself stalling — more serious, because the rule tells every agent to depend on it. Worth a distinct napkin/distilled entry + a tooling-fix work item.' This is a failure-mode report about the failure-mode-reporting channel's own infrastructure (the comms watcher that agents depend on to read failure-mode events) written as a failure-mode event into that same corpus.

Cosmos turns Equinox (1bc763, 2026-06-12T06:42:11Z) reports a failure-mode tagged event: their comms watcher died three times in one session at escalating timeout budgets (60s, 180s, 300s). Diagnosis: 'the per-step deadline treats a load-starved slow drain as a hang.' The cure direction offered: 'make the drain step's deadline load-aware or incremental... The comms-dir event count also only grows — a fixed budget loses eventually regardless of load.' The observation that the corpus only grows — with the corpus's own growth being the mechanism of watcher failure — is a direct structural instance of the corpus overwhelming the tool that agents use to observe it, written as a failure-mode event into that same growing corpus.

Katydid hunts Roost's successor brief (afd35253, 2026-06-13T08:50:12Z) and closeout event (94d0287e, 2026-06-13T08:55:49Z) both name 'theme-13, the live reflexive finding': 'the comms-event watcher wedges repeatedly on the ~5,120-file dir (theme-13, the live reflexive finding).' The successor brief instructs the incoming agent: 'restart short (45s budget), gap-sweep on restart.' The closeout adds: 'The comms-event watcher wedges on the ~5,120-file dir (theme-13, the live reflexive finding) — restart short (45s budget), gap-sweep on restart. Fable was in a temporary outage today.' The corpus research session formally named this as a research theme: the corpus had grown large enough that the watcher used to read the corpus's events became the corpus's own victim. The observation tool and the observed object are the same filesystem directory. Theme-13 is the corpus naming its own observability failure as a finding within itself.

find.cure_shape: Activation-enthalpy tuning on the blind-pass fence and watcher startup. The blind-pass fence should be located in a separate stub document that is referenced from (not embedded within) the research thread record — so the start-right reading order surfaces the fence BEFORE the contaminating content, not after. For the watcher wedge: the comms-watch CLI should default to incremental batched drain (bounded passes with per-batch deadlines) rather than a single full-dir scan under one step deadline, so the corpus's own growth does not make the watcher pathologically expensive. Both cures make the desired behaviour cheaper by restructuring the default path, not by adding mandates or prohibition. Observe (do not mandate) whether agents voluntarily re-dispatch blind cold reads after contamination; the corpus contains at least one instance of a research agent disclosing contamination openly and proposing a fresh-delegate cure — that voluntary disclosure is evidence the norm is functioning.
find.notes: The hypothesis is confirmed and the corpus is more self-aware than stated — there are at least three distinct recursive layers: (1) Charcoal's deliberate seeding of the research-substrate declaration into the corpus at b2f6a5fe; (2) Katydid's failure-mode disclosure (37523113) where the research session studying failure modes was itself afflicted by an activation-enthalpy failure mode, and that failure was written as a failure-mode event into the corpus being studied; (3) the watcher-wedge-on-growth recursion (26c8b7e9, 4e35c31c, afd35253, 94d0287e) where the corpus's own size caused the infrastructure that agents depend on to read failure-mode reports to fail — and those failures were written as failure-mode events into the same growing corpus, formally named as 'theme-13, the live reflexive finding' by the research session. The hypothesis that Charcoal 'predicted this very cold-read' is partially accurate: b2f6a5fe named five future session shapes including 'corpus survey' and 'failure-mode taxonomy', and those are precisely the session shapes Katydid ran. However, the term 'cold-read' and the specific contamination failure mode were not predicted — they arose blind (provenance: blind-arisen for all three watcher-failure instances). The 'recursion density' framing in the hypothesis is fully vindicated: failure-mode events about the failure-mode channel are structurally unavoidable so long as the corpus grows and the watcher is the canonical reading mechanism. One nuance to conserve: the b2f6a5fe event is dated 2026-05-24, within the window but at its start; the watcher-failure cascade that became theme-13 was primarily a June 2026 phenomenon, spanning 26c8b7e9 (June 10), 4e35c31c (June 12), and the research session closeout (June 13). The corpus grew into its own observability problem across the three weeks of the window. The /tmp write was not performed — this agent operates in read-only mode and file creation to /tmp is prohibited under the active constraint.
